anchors.paper_title: Large-scale training data enhances silent speech decoding with around-ear EEG
anchors.reason: The paper title and abstract specifically discuss the use and evaluation of around-ear EEG data for silent speech decoding, directly relating to the EEG-Speech Brain Decoding Dataset.

metadata.methods_description: EEG data were acquired using three different systems: g.tec g.Pangolin (128 EEG channels), g.tec g.SCARABEO (64 EEG-related channels), and ANT Neuro eego sports (63 EEG channels). All recordings included supplementary channels for audio monitoring, electrooculography (EOG), electromyography (EMG), and trigger signals. Three experimental tasks were performed: speechopen (overt speech production with visually presented text), listening (passive auditory listening to prerecorded speech), and listeningcovert (auditory listening followed by covert speech imagery). Sessions are organized by recording date (YYYYMMDD format) with multiple runs distinguished by run numbers.

citation_details.title: Bio-integrated systems for silent speech recognition: from advanced bioplatforms to machine learning-assisted biosignal decoding
citation_details.author: Penghao Dong, Yuanqing Song, Yizong Li, Petar M. Djurić, Shanshan Yao
citation_details.abstract: Silent speech interfaces decode intended speech from physiological signals without the need for vocalized sound. These systems provide an alternative modality to voice-based spoken communication, addressing limitations posed by physiological constraints and environmental interferences. This review presents a comprehensive overview of bio-integrated systems for silent speech recognition, with emphasis on their physiological relevance, state-of-the-art hardware designs, signal characteristics, and machine learning (ML)-assisted speech decoding pipelines. Based on the level of physical intrusion into the body, bio-integrated speech interfaces can be categorized into epidermal, intraoral, and surgically embedded systems. Each modality captures distinct physiological signals involved in speech production.
